scout.purpose: Turn providers, properties, and build inputs into a predictable, testable build-system contract.
scout.realWorldUse: Large Android builds must produce trustworthy variants quickly across developer machines and CI while tooling and module graphs evolve.
scout.outcome: Model the build behaviour, implement it with lazy public APIs, and verify correctness plus performance.

blocks.text: Provider represents a read-only value available later; Property adds configurable assignment and conventions. RegularFileProperty, DirectoryProperty, ListProperty, SetProperty and MapProperty retain type and producer information. Wire values with map, flatMap, zip and set(provider), rather than converting early to String or File. A convention supplies a default that a consumer may override, while finalization APIs can freeze a value once configuration is complete. This model removes fragile evaluation-order assumptions from build logic.

blocks.text: Read project properties, environment variables and files through providerFactory where possible so Gradle can track configuration inputs. Do not call System.getenv in task actions without declaring the result, and do not hide release-affecting state in global singletons. Secrets should be passed only to tasks that need them, marked sensitive in surrounding CI, excluded from logs and never declared as cacheable outputs. Distinguish a value that changes generated bytes from operational values such as heap size that do not affect output identity.

blocks.caption: A focused build fragment; its full correctness depends on declared inputs, lifecycle, compatibility and functional evidence.

blocks.text: Provider chains also preserve automatic task dependencies: a generated file’s Provider knows its producer. Validate missing inputs with clear errors at the latest useful boundary, not by forcing every value during configuration. Use finalizeValue or disallowChanges when late mutation would make the model ambiguous. Functional tests should cover defaults, explicit overrides, absent values and configuration-cache reuse. Lazy does not mean unpredictable; it means the graph records how to calculate a value when its consumer needs it.

Build logic is production infrastructure: it shapes every developer feedback loop and release artifact. Make ownership, inputs, outputs, compatibility, security boundaries, failure messages, metrics and rollback explicit. Prefer public typed APIs, lazy Provider wiring and deterministic isolated tasks. Verify the model through representative local and CI workflows, clean and incremental changes, parallel execution, relocated workspaces, configuration-cache reuse and trusted build-cache restoration. Measure before optimising, then preserve correctness with functional tests and regression budgets. Avoid hidden environment state, internal APIs, task-name guessing, global project mutation, mutable network inputs and credentials in logs or reusable outputs. Record the supported Gradle, AGP, Kotlin, Java and operating-system matrix, and make upgrades controlled experiments with safe rollback evidence. A fast build is valuable only when it produces the right traceable artifact consistently.

blocks.title: Common build trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Calling provider.get at plugin application time defeats deferred calculation and can make unrelated commands fail because an optional value is absent.

trap_check.mistake: Calling provider.get at plugin application time defeats deferred calculation and can make unrelated commands fail because an optional value is absent.
trap_check.why: The build may become eager, stale, nondeterministic, incorrectly variant-aware or unsafe under parallel and cached execution.
trap_check.fix: Use the public model, declare the complete data flow and add a functional regression test.

trap_check.mistake: Optimising a synthetic clean build without measuring the team’s frequent workflow.
trap_check.why: The change can shift cost or complexity without improving developer or CI feedback.
trap_check.fix: Baseline representative workflows and compare controlled before/after critical paths.

challenge_intro.task: Create a typed extension whose conventions feed two task inputs through Provider transformations, then test override, absence, finalisation and configuration-cache behaviour.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The build behaviour is correct for clean, incremental, parallel and cached paths and has measured evidence, diagnostics and ownership.

recall.prompt: What does flatMap preserve that reading a file path early can lose?
recall.answer: Lazy calculation and producer dependency information carried by the nested Provider.

recall.prompt: What makes custom Gradle work trustworthy?
recall.answer: Complete declared inputs and outputs, deterministic isolated execution, lazy wiring, public APIs and functional tests.

recall.prompt: What should precede a build-performance change?
recall.answer: A representative workflow, controlled baseline and evidence locating the critical path or avoidable work.
